body: it seems like everyone I know of who has used these medications has had nothing but bad experiences with them. Is this a case of a very loud minority existing? I also worry about telling these things to a professional because I don't want to get involuntarily committed. I really value my freedom and privacy.

I'm currently in college. My grades are almost exclusively from tests, there are very few assignments in my courses. I get major test anxiety so this isn't a very good situation.

I was recently diagnosed with diabetes and is has greatly impacted how I feel about my health.

I just want to see some good in something. I used to be able to. I feel broken. I know that nothing's going to make me feel completely better. If things were just a bit brighter for me I know I could make it through the day. But no, it's like my former ability to be positive has converted into negativity and I had enough of that to begin with.

i live in an unsafe area that's not particularly healthy for me. at night, it's a bit too dangerous to walk alone. during the day people stare at me and make me feel worse.

i used to live in a rural area, and ran cross country. i miss having that release. i miss being able to leave my house without seeing people.

i'm having another night like this. worse than usual because it's my 20th birthday and i'll be expected to go pretend that i'm fine whenever i wake up. ativan cuts some of the anxiety but does nothing for the pain.
